newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends softer, LME stock hike expected.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends softer, LME stock hike expected.

text.p: COMEX copper ended slightly down ahead of an expected hike in LME stocks Tuesday, but the market will remain firm as long as the backwardation in London is strong, traders said.

A hike of 6,000 to 8,000 tonnes in LME stocks was anticipated by dealers, as the strong backwardation attracted metal into depots, and the LME spot premium over COMEX spawned a further rash of arbitrage-related metal flows in the U.S.
Tight dates on LME from Jan 29 to mid-February, reflected in the backwardation, were now coming into play, and traders were waiting to see what became of the backwardation once these dates are past.
"My concern is that when the backwardation comes in, it will come in rather sharply with the spot month coming down sharply with it," said John Gross of the Copper Journal.
"But despite the rises in inventories, they are still very low, and we do have a potential for another squeeze," Gross said.
Most-active March COMEX copper went out 0.75 cent lower at 105.90 cents a lb, traded 107.65 to 105.75 cents, still within its recent trading range.
Spot January, which goes off the board Wednesday, ended 0.20 cent firmer at 111.20 cents.
Volume was estimated at 7,500 lots compared to Friday's official 9,755 lots.

Traders said the strong backwardation and tightness on LME was partly justifiable due to low stocks and strong demand, particularly in the United States, but its strength was exacerbated by speculative trading.
